newsitem.title: USA: United Airlines pilots ratify wage pact.
newsitem.headline: United Airlines pilots ratify wage pact.

text.p: UAL Corp said Thursday that United Airlines' pilots union members approved a mid-contract wage agreement reached last month with the nation's largest airline.
The Air Line Pilots Association said 98 percent of its members ratified the pact, with 90 percent of its members casting votes.
The proposal offers two mid-term wage increases of five percent, with the first effective in July and the second effective in July 1998.

In the year 2000, the pact also restore wage rates to levels that existed before July 1994, when certain United employees agreed to wage reductions in exchange for an ownership stake in the company. United's employees own 55 percent of UAL Corp's common stock.

At the conclusion of the Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP), United's contribution to the pilots' pension fund will also be restored to pre-ESOP levels of nine percent, up from the current level of one percent.
United's machinists union ratified a similar proposal last month.

In February, United's 8,500 pilots rejected a previous wage proposal that would have increase pay by 10 percent over four year. The mechanics' union, which represents more than 12,000 workers, also rejected a similar proposal in early January.
The approval of the contracts puts to rest the bulk of the labor concerns at the airline. United is currently conducting contract talks in Hawaii with its flight attendants union.
